title: उत्तरपर्व · अध्याय १८७

items.text:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
अथातः संप्रवक्ष्यामि तव पांडुकुलोद्वह ॥
पुण्यं हेमरथं नाम महापातकनाशनम् ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
|| śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca || ||
athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi tava pāṃḍukulodvaha ||
puṇyaṃ hemarathaṃ nāma mahāpātakanāśanam || 1 ||

items.text:
पुण्येऽह्नि विप्रकथिते स्वनुलिप्ते गृहांगणे ॥
कृष्णाजिनतिलान्कृत्वा कांचनं स्थापयेद्रथम् ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
puṇye'hni viprakathite svanulipte gṛhāṃgaṇe ||
kṛṣṇājinatilānkṛtvā kāṃcanaṃ sthāpayedratham || 2 ||

items.text:
चतुरस्रं महाभाग चतुश्चक्रं सकूबरम् ॥
ब्रह्माणमग्रतः कृत्वा गृहीतप्रग्रहं शुभम् ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
caturasraṃ mahābhāga catuścakraṃ sakūbaram ||
brahmāṇamagrataḥ kṛtvā gṛhītapragrahaṃ śubham || 3 ||

items.text:
इंद्रनीलेन कुंभेन ध्वजरूपेण संयुतम् ॥
लोकपालाष्टकोपेतं पद्मरागदलान्वितम् ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
iṃdranīlena kuṃbhena dhvajarūpeṇa saṃyutam ||
lokapālāṣṭakopetaṃ padmarāgadalānvitam || 4 ||

items.text:
मध्ये तु फलसंयुक्तं पुरुषेण समन्वितम् ॥
योगयुक्तः पुमान्कार्यस्तं च तत्राधिवासयेत् ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
madhye tu phalasaṃyuktaṃ puruṣeṇa samanvitam ||
yogayuktaḥ pumānkāryastaṃ ca tatrādhivāsayet || 6 ||

items.text:
एवंविधं पूजयित्वा माल्यगंधानुलेपनैः ॥
चक्ररक्षावुभौ तस्य कार्यौ विश्वकुमारकौ ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃvidhaṃ pūjayitvā mālyagaṃdhānulepanaiḥ ||
cakrarakṣāvubhau tasya kāryau viśvakumārakau || 7 ||

items.text:
पुण्यं कालं ततः प्राप्य स्नातः संपूज्य देवताः ॥
त्रिःप्रदक्षिणमावृत्य गृहीतकुसुमांजलिः ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
puṇyaṃ kālaṃ tataḥ prāpya snātaḥ saṃpūjya devatāḥ ||
triḥpradakṣiṇamāvṛtya gṛhītakusumāṃjaliḥ || 6 ||

items.text:
नमोनमः पापविनाशनाय विश्वात्मने देवतुरंगमाय ॥
धात्रामधीशाय भवाभवाय रथस्य दानान्मम देहि शांतिम् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
namonamaḥ pāpavināśanāya viśvātmane devaturaṃgamāya ||
dhātrāmadhīśāya bhavābhavāya rathasya dānānmama dehi śāṃtim || 10 ||

items.text:
वस्वष्टकादित्यमरुद्गणानां त्वमेव धाता परमं निधानम् ॥
यतस्ततो मे हृदयं प्रयातु धर्मैकतानत्वमघौघनाशात् ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
vasvaṣṭakādityamarudgaṇānāṃ tvameva dhātā paramaṃ nidhānam ||
yatastato me hṛdayaṃ prayātu dharmaikatānatvamaghaughanāśāt || 11 ||

items.text:
इति तुरगरथप्रदानमेतद्भवभयसूदनमंत्रं यः करोति ॥
सकलुषपटलैर्विमुक्तदेहः परममुपैति पदं पिनाकपाणेः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
iti turagarathapradānametadbhavabhayasūdanamaṃtraṃ yaḥ karoti ||
sakaluṣapaṭalairvimuktadehaḥ paramamupaiti padaṃ pinākapāṇeḥ || 12 ||

items.text:
देदीप्यमानवपुषा च जितप्रभावमाक्रम्य मडलमखंडलचंडभानोः ॥
सिद्धांगनानयनयुग्मप्रनि पीयमानवक्त्रांबुजेंऽबुजभवेन चिरं सहास्ते ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
dedīpyamānavapuṣā ca jitaprabhāvamākramya maḍalamakhaṃḍalacaṃḍabhānoḥ ||
siddhāṃganānayanayugmaprani pīyamānavaktrāṃbujeṃ'bujabhavena ciraṃ sahāste || 13 ||

items.text:
इति पठति शृणोति वा य एतत्कनकतुरंगरथप्रदानमस्मिन् ॥
न स नरकपुरं व्रजेत्कदाचिन्नरकरिपोर्भवनं प्रयाति भूयः ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya etatkanakaturaṃgarathapradānamasmin ||
na sa narakapuraṃ vrajetkadācinnarakariporbhavanaṃ prayāti bhūyaḥ || 14 ||

items.h: इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराण उत्तरपर्वणि श्रीकृष्णयुधिष्ठिरसंवादे हिरण्याश्वरथदानविधिवर्णनं नाम सप्ताशीत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ।। १८७ ।।

en_summary: Krishna gives the gold chariot (hema-ratha), which destroys the great sins. On a holy day named by Brahmins, in a well-plastered courtyard, a square four-wheeled gold chariot with a pole is set on sesame over a black antelope skin, with Brahma in front holding the reins, a sapphire pot as its flag, the eight world guardians and ruby petals, four full pots, the eighteen grains, a silk cover and canopy, and in the middle, with fruits, a figure of a man sitting in yoga; two Vishvakumaras are made as guards of its wheels. It is worshipped with garlands, perfumes and sandal, and at the holy time the bathed patron, having worshipped the gods, walks around it three times in white with flowers and prays: "Again and again homage to you, destroyer of sin, soul of the universe, horse of the gods, lord of the creators, cause of being and not being; by the gift of this chariot give me peace; you are the creator and highest treasure of the eight Vasus, the Adityas and the Maruts; so, with my flood of sins destroyed, may my heart turn wholly to dharma." The giver, freed of sin, reaches the highest abode of Shiva, the bearer of Pinaka; shining in body, he passes beyond the sun's disc and lives long with Brahma, his lotus face drunk in by the eyes of siddha women. One who reads or hears of this gift of the gold horse chariot never goes to hell and goes again to the home of Krishna, the enemy of Naraka.
